extracted.intended_audience: Heads of Executive Departments and Establishments; federal agency managers responsible for facility/parking policy
extracted.subtask_description: Draft OMB circular establishing policy and fees for use of Federal government parking lots, including carpooling requirements, fee structure, exemptions, phase-in, and managerial obligations. Intended to guide agency implementation and solicit written comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish fees for use of certain government parking lots
rubrics_metrics.description: Attached draft circular intended to establish fees for the use of certain government parking lots; agencies are to implement pricing for Federal parking where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General instruction that a parking fee regime be established and applied to certain Federal installations; solicits comments on the draft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy aligned with energy conservation and public transit objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy should be consistent with national policies toward energy conservation, reliance on public transportation and a cleaner environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: subsidizing parking is inconsistent with energy-conscious era; pricing should encourage reduced automobile use and greater transit reliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charge commercially equivalent fees to reduce automobile use
rubrics_metrics.description: Charging commercially equivalent fees for parking would reduce the number of cars in urban cores and increase carpooling and transit use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supported by regional studies (Washington Metropolitan Area Council of Governments, Los Angeles comparative study) that link parking cost to automobile use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee basis — fair monthly rental value
rubrics_metrics.description: The circular would establish a parking fee at all Federal installations based on the fair monthly rental value of the parking space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees are to reflect commercial rental value rather than arbitrary nominal amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption threshold: no fee if rental value under $10/month
rubrics_metrics.description: No fee will be charged in most cases where the rental value is less than $10.00 per month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A de minimis exemption to avoid charging where commercial-equivalent value is very low.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee level intent: recover space costs and incentivize carpooling
rubrics_metrics.description: Intent is to set a fee high enough to recover space costs and act as an incentive to carpooling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance desired: fee should discourage single-occupant driving while reflecting actual space costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid administrative costs consuming fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees should not be set so low that administration of a fee system and parking management would totally consume the fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider administrative overhead when setting fee levels; very low fees are counterproductive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase-in period for adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: The circular provides for a phase-in period to help employees and agencies adjust carpooling and financial arrangements as necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gradual implementation to allow time for behavioral and logistical changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managerial obligation when parking remains free
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency managers at locations which would continue to provide parking without charge must develop and implement affirmative plans for maximizing carpooling and vanpooling among employees and other building tenants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even where no fee is charged, agencies must proactively promote shared-ride options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeting: downtown and densely populated suburban focus
rubrics_metrics.description: The pricing policy will primarily affect Federal facilities in downtown locations and densely populated suburban locations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect greater application in high-rent/ high-demand areas where commercial-equivalent rents justify fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stricter application of carpooling requirements government-wide
rubrics_metrics.description: More stringent application of carpooling requirements will affect all locations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not limited to downtowns; carpooling rules should be applied uniformly and more rigorously across installations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform application of carpooling regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Government-wide carpooling regulations are not uniformly applied; the circular implies a need for more consistent enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must ensure carpooling regulations meet intended utilization targets (discussion cites 90% objective in Washington core).

rubrics_metrics.name: Utilization objective: high carpool usage in urban core
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulation's objective cited of 90 percent utilization by carpools in the core of the Washington, D.C. area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides an explicit utilization target to measure success of carpool policies in core areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected outcomes / evaluation metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Expected benefits include considerable cost savings to the taxpayer, reduced energy consumption, less traffic congestion, increased transit use, greater carpooling and improved air quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These outcomes serve as evaluation criteria for the policy's effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize hardship and provide alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: In the vast majority of cases charging a commercial-rate for parking is not expected to impose a hardship; employees will often be able to share costs through carpooling or use public transit as a cost-effective option.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy design should consider employee hardship and promote mitigations (carpools, transit) where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence-based justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy references studies relating automobile use to the cost of parking (e.g., Washington Metropolitan Area Council of Governments, Los Angeles comparative study) as support for charging fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy should be grounded in empirical studies showing behavioral effects of parking pricing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation of written comments (notice-and-comment procedural requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Draft invites written comments to Ms. Joyce Walker, Deputy Associate Director, Room 9202, OMB, Washington, D.C. 20503, no later than April 30, 1979.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides explicit submission instructions and a deadline as part of the rulemaking/consultation process.
